question: Tell me about a time you proactively sought feedback, training, or development to improve.

raiseTranscript.text: After shipping my first feature, I asked two senior engineers for a detailed code review even though it wasn't required. They pointed out several patterns I could improve.
I spent the next sprint refactoring the module using their suggestions and asked them to review the changes again. My error rate on similar tasks dropped.

raiseNotes: Q: Tell me about a time you proactively sought feedback, training, or development to improve.
Role: new grad on first feature; asked seniors for extra code review
Actions: implemented feedback, requested second review, measured improvement
Outcome: reduced errors on follow-on work
Quote: "I asked two senior engineers for a detailed code review even though it wasn't required."
Follow-up: What did you do next? → Refactored and asked for re-review
junior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar on Initiative for a junior. Candidate independently requested extra code review after their first feature and acted on the input by refactoring, directly reducing errors on later tasks. The story shows ownership of personal skill growth without waiting for a manager prompt. Biggest strength is the closed loop of seeking, applying, and verifying feedback on their own work.

We aligned on a shared contract and I ran a brown-bag for my team. Cross-team incidents dropped 40% over the next quarter.

raiseNotes: Q: Tell me about a time you proactively sought feedback, training, or development to improve.

Actions: scheduled review, aligned on contract, taught team
Outcome: 40% drop in cross-team incidents
Quote: "I asked their tech lead for a 1:1 to review our API usage patterns."

senior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar on Initiative for a senior. Candidate spotted recurring cross-team friction and proactively sought feedback from another team's lead, then drove alignment and knowledge sharing that produced a measurable 40% reduction in incidents. Shows influence without authority and impact beyond their immediate team. Biggest strength is turning personal outreach into team-level improvement.

raiseTranscript.text: My team's on-call load was causing burnout, so I asked two peer managers for their runbook and escalation processes.
How did that affect your team?
I adapted their model, trained my leads on it, and rotated ownership. Attrition risk signals fell and two engineers later told me they felt more supported.

raiseNotes: Q: Tell me about a time you proactively sought feedback, training, or development to improve.

Actions: adapted process, trained leads, measured signals
Outcome: reduced attrition risk, engineers reported feeling supported
